title: Erdős Problem #16: Odd Integers Not of Form 2^k + p
description: Is the set of odd integers not of the form 2^k + p the union of an arithmetic progression and a density-0 set? DISPROVED by Chen (2023).

meta.author: Romanoff (1934), Erdős (1950), Chen (2023)

relatedProblems.relationship: Both concern the distribution of primes: Bertrand's postulate guarantees primes in intervals, while Problem #16 asks about representing odd numbers as 2^k + p
The prime density results underlying Romanoff's theorem (positive proportion of odd integers are 2^k + p) depend on prime counting estimates
Both are solved Erdős problems in analytic number theory with density/measure-theoretic conclusions

meta.assumptions: This file states the problem (definitions IsRomanoff, ExceptionalSet, density, lowerDensity, IsCoveringSystem, ErdosConjecture16, erdosCovering, and the related Props Erdos9/10/11Question) and proves 13 axiom-free foundational lemmas about those definitions. It contains 0 axioms and 0 sorries. The deep results (Romanoff 1934 positive density, Erdos 1950 covering construction, Chen 2023 disproof) require analytic number theory beyond current Mathlib and remain described in doc-comments only, NOT formalized as theorems or axioms. The formalized lemmas are elementary structural facts: the Romanoff floor (2^k+p >= 4), concrete Romanoff witnesses (5=2+3, 7=4+3), membership of 1 and 3 in the exceptional set, the 0<=density<=1 range, and a full machine-checked proof that the explicit Erdos covering system {0 mod 2, 0 mod 3, 1 mod 4, 1 mod 6, 3 mod 8, 7 mod 12, 23 mod 24} genuinely covers the integers. Session 3 adds a finite-range refinement isRomanoff_iff_mem_range (the witness exponent lies in Finset.range n since 2^k<n forces k<2^k<n), a Decidable (IsRomanoff n) instance derived from it (kernel reduction only, no native_decide), and two further A006285 terms proved exceptional: 251 (249=3·83, 247=13·19, 243=3^5, 235=5·47, 219=3·73, 187=11·17, 123=3·41 all composite) and 331 (329=7·47, 327=3·109, 323=17·19, 315=5·63, 299=13·23, 267=3·89, 203=7·29, 75=3·25 all composite). Still 0 axioms, 0 sorries. Session 4 formalizes the covering-congruence OBSTRUCTION mechanism behind Erdos's 1950 argument (5 new axiom-free theorems, still 0 axioms/0 sorries): two_pow_mod_three (order of 2 mod 3 is 2: 2^k%3 = 1 if k even else 2), two_pow_modEq_of_dvd (the core algebraic gear: if 2^d = 1 mod p and k = r mod d then 2^k = 2^r mod p), covering_prime_not_prime_sub (the general obstruction: given a prime p with 2^d = 1 mod p, an exponent k = r mod d, and n = 2^r mod p, then p divides n-2^k, so n-2^k is composite whenever it exceeds p — this is exactly how one residue class of exponents is eliminated), and two concrete gears not_prime_sub_even_mod_three (prime 3 kills even exponents for n = 1 mod 3) and not_prime_sub_mod_seven (prime 7 kills exponents divisible by 3 for n = 1 mod 7). Assembling all gears over a full covering system into a single arithmetic progression via CRT remains the deep step (documented only). Session 5 assembles the gears into the full covering obstruction covering_obstruction_not_isRomanoff (8 new axiom-free theorems, still 0 axioms/0 sorries): the four remaining order-of-2 gears 2^4=1 mod 5, 2^8=1 mod 17, 2^12=1 mod 13, 2^24=1 mod 241 (the primes closing the exponent classes k=1 mod 4, k=3 mod 8, k=7 mod 12, k=23 mod 24), then a single theorem showing that any n meeting the six CRT congruences n=1 mod 3, n=1 mod 7, n=2 mod 5, n=8 mod 17, n=11 mod 13, n=121 mod 241 and the size condition n-2^k>241 for every exponent k with 2^k<n is NOT Romanoff, because each exponent falls into one of the six covering classes {0 mod 2, 0 mod 3, 1 mod 4, 3 mod 8, 7 mod 12, 23 mod 24} whose attached prime divides n-2^k. The membership corollary covering_progression_mem_exceptionalSet gives n in ExceptionalSet for odd such n. This is Erdos's 1950 covering-congruence construction in full, formalized as an unconditional obstruction subject to a single explicit size hypothesis. Session 6 discharges the remaining analytic wrapper at full strength (7 new axiom-free theorems/defs, still 0 axioms/0 sorries): coveringAP (the covering progression 7629217 + q*11184810) and Trapped (n within 241 of a smaller power of two) set up coveringAP_mem_exceptionalSet, which shows every untrapped progression member is exceptional; card_trapped_le bounds how many progression members below a horizon can be trapped (at most one per dyadic window, so at most log2 N + 1 total); exceptionalCount_lower_bound and exceptionalCount_positive_density combine these to show at least N/11184810 - (log2 N + 1) exceptional integers lie below N, which for N >= 2^52 exceeds N/22369620 -- a positive proportion. density_exceptionalSet_ge and lowerDensity_exceptionalSet_pos package this as 0 < lowerDensity ExceptionalSet, superseding the earlier exceptionalSet_infinite with Erdos's 1950 result at full strength: not just infinitely many exceptional integers, but a positive proportion of them. Still 0 axioms, 0 sorries. What remains documented-only is Romanoff's 1934 positive-density theorem for the complementary set and Chen's 2023 disproof of the conjecture.

overview.historicalContext: Romanoff (1934) proved that the set $\{n : n = 2^k + p\}$ has positive lower density among odd integers, using sieve methods and the prime number theorem to show that the 'expected count' of representations diverges. Erdős (1950) turned to the complementary question: what does the exceptional set $E$ look like? His key tool was covering congruences — systems of residue classes $\{a_i \pmod{m_i}\}$ that tile $\mathbb{Z}$. By choosing moduli $\{2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24\}$ (whose reciprocals sum to 1), Erdős arranged that for any $n$ in a particular residue class mod $\text{lcm} = 24$, each $n - 2^k$ is divisible by a small prime. This forced an infinite AP into $E$. Erdős then conjectured — self-deprecatingly calling it 'rather silly' — that $E$ is essentially just this AP plus density-0 noise. After 73 years, Chen (2023) disproved this by showing $E$ contains infinitely many essentially independent APs, each contributing positive density. The exceptional set's structure is far richer than a single covering congruence produces.
overview.problemStatement: Define the exceptional set E = {odd n : n ≠ 2^k + p for all k ≥ 1 and primes p}. Erdős asked: is E = (arithmetic progression) ∪ (density-0 set)? Chen proved NO: E has more complex structure.
overview.text: Is the set of odd integers not of the form 2^k + p the union of an arithmetic progression and a density-0 set? DISPROVED by Chen (2023).
overview.proofStrategy: Defines Romanoff numbers (n = 2^k + p, k>=1, p prime), the exceptional set, covering congruence systems, density/lowerDensity, ErdosConjecture16, and the related Props for Problems #9-#11. Adds 13 axiom-free foundational lemmas: isRomanoff_four_le (structural lower bound via 2^k>=2 and p>=2), not_isRomanoff_one/three and one/three_mem_exceptionalSet (small odd numbers are exceptional), isRomanoff_five/seven (concrete witnesses), density_nonneg/density_le_one (range of the density functional), erdosCovering_moduli_pos, and erdosCovering_isCoveringSystem (the explicit covering system covers Z, proved by reducing mod 24 via omega and exhibiting the residue-class witness). Romanoff's theorem, Erdos's covering-progression result, and Chen's disproof appear in documentation only and are not formalized.
keyInsights: 127 is exceptional: 127 - 2^k is composite for all valid k
Erdős's covering system: moduli {2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24} ensure composites
E has positive density ~0.09 (from the arithmetic progression)
Chen (2023): E is NOT just one AP + density-0 noise
E contains infinitely many 'independent' progressions with positive density
Erdős's 1950 covering progression gives a machine-checked lower bound: at least N/22369620 exceptional integers below every N ≥ 2^52, i.e. a positive lower density, not just infinitude

sections.title: Core Definitions
sections.summary: Defines `IsRomanoff n` ($\exists k \geq 1, p$ prime: $n = 2^k + p$), `ExceptionalSet` (odd non-Romanoff integers), and documents (not formalized) the characterization that $n$ is exceptional iff $n - 2^k$ is composite for every valid $k$.

sections.title: The Romanoff Theorem
sections.summary: Defines asymptotic `density` and `lowerDensity`, then documents (not formalized) Romanoff's theorem: the Romanoff numbers have positive lower density among odd integers. Corollary: the exceptional set has density less than $1/2$.

sections.summary: Defines `IsCoveringSystem` and documents (not formalized) Erdős's 1950 result: using covering congruences with moduli $\{2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24\}$, the exceptional set contains an infinite arithmetic progression.

sections.title: The Conjecture and Its Disproof
sections.summary: Formalizes `ErdosConjecture16`: $E = (\text{AP}) \cup (\text{density-0 set})$. Documents (not formalized) Chen's 2023 disproof (stated as ¬ErdosConjecture16; no such declaration exists in the source) and the consequence that no single AP captures $E$ up to density 0.

sections.title: Why Chen's Result is Significant
sections.summary: Prose: Chen's 2023 disproof shows the exceptional set has rich structure beyond a single arithmetic progression — possibly multiple independent progressions, fractal/quasi-random behaviour, and deep ties to prime distribution.
sections.mathContext: Motivates the disproof: the exceptional set is not (AP) ∪ (density-0), suggesting genuinely multi-progression / quasi-random structure.

sections.title: Foundational Lemmas (Axiom-Free)
sections.summary: The machine-checked core (0 axioms): mem_exceptionalSet_iff, isRomanoff_four_le, not_isRomanoff_one/three and membership of 1,3 in the exceptional set; Romanoff witnesses isRomanoff_five/seven with five_not_mem_exceptionalSet; density_nonneg / density_le_one; erdosCovering_moduli_pos and erdosCovering_isCoveringSystem (the {2,3,4,6,8,12,24} system genuinely covers ℤ, by decide); the bounded characterisation isRomanoff_iff / isRomanoff_iff_mem_range with the resulting IsRomanoff Decidable instance; and verified exceptionality of the OEIS A006285 terms 127, 149, 251, 331.

Key device: $\texttt{isRomanoff\_iff\_mem\_range}$ bounds the witness exponent $k$ to a finite range, making $\texttt{IsRomanoff}$ decidable and the exceptionality of 127/149/251/331 machine-checkable by `decide`.

sections.title: The Covering-Congruence Obstruction Mechanism (Axiom-Free)
sections.summary: The verified gear behind the covering construction: two_pow_mod_three (2^k mod 3 is periodic with period 2), two_pow_modEq_of_dvd (order-periodicity of 2 mod p), the general obstruction covering_prime_not_prime_sub (if p | n − 2^k on a residue class then n − 2^k is composite there), and the concrete gears not_prime_sub_even_mod_three (prime 3, even exponents) and not_prime_sub_mod_seven (prime 7, exponents ≡ 0 mod 3). All axiom-free.
sections.mathContext: Formalizes how a covering system forces compositeness: fixing a prime $p$ and exponent period $d$, on the residue class where $p \mid n - 2^k$ the value $n-2^k$ is divisible by $p$ yet exceeds it, so it is not prime — the mechanism producing an AP of exceptional $n$.

sections.title: Assembling the Gears: The Full Covering Obstruction (Axiom-Free)
sections.summary: Runs the full covering system of the *exponent*: the six classes k ≡ 0 (2), 0 (3), 1 (4), 3 (8), 7 (12), 23 (24) cover ℤ, each closed by a prime whose order of 2 equals that modulus — 3, 7, 5, 17, 13, 241. The order gears two_pow_two_modEq_three, two_pow_three_modEq_seven, two_pow_four_modEq_five, two_pow_eight_modEq_seventeen, two_pow_twelve_modEq_thirteen, two_pow_twentyfour_modEq_241 (all by decide/norm_num) supply the third table column. The assembled theorem covering_obstruction_not_isRomanoff shows any n meeting the six residues n ≡ 1(3),1(7),2(5),8(17),11(13),121(241) and the size hypothesis (n − 2^k > 241 for all valid k) is not Romanoff, and covering_progression_mem_exceptionalSet packages the odd such n as members of ExceptionalSet — the membership form of Erdős's 1950 theorem that the exceptional set contains a full CRT arithmetic progression mod 3·5·7·13·17·241. All axiom-free.
sections.mathContext: Six primes with $\text{ord}_p(2)=d$ close a covering system of the exponent $k$; by CRT the progression $n \equiv a \pmod{3\cdot5\cdot7\cdot13\cdot17\cdot241}$ (odd, large) makes every $n-2^k$ composite, so the whole progression lies in $\text{ExceptionalSet}$ — Erdős (1950), assembled unconditionally modulo one explicit size hypothesis.

sections.title: Erdős's Infinite Arithmetic Progression: The Exceptional Set is Infinite
sections.summary: Promotes the CRT membership form into an unconditional infinitude result. exists_exceptional_gt: for every bound B there is an exceptional n > B, obtained by picking a member of the covering progression large enough that the size hypothesis (n − 2^k composite for every valid k) holds inside the confining window. exceptionalSet_infinite: ExceptionalSet.Infinite follows immediately, since arbitrarily large exceptional integers exist — the full Erdős (1950) theorem that infinitely many odd numbers are not of the form 2^k + p, proved axiom-free.
sections.mathContext: From the covering progression modulo $3\cdot5\cdot7\cdot13\cdot17\cdot241$ one extracts, above any bound $B$, an odd $n$ with every $n-2^k$ composite; hence $\text{ExceptionalSet}$ is unbounded and therefore infinite (Erdős 1950), with no axioms.

sections.title: Erdős (1950), Full Strength: The Exceptional Set Has Positive Lower Density
sections.summary: Strengthens infinitude to positive lower density, all axiom-free. coveringAP (the explicit progression 7629217 + q·11184810) and Trapped (n within 241 of a smaller power of two) feed coveringAP_mem_exceptionalSet (every untrapped member is exceptional); card_trapped_le bounds trapped members below a horizon N by the number of relevant powers of two (at most log₂ N + 1, since each dyadic window traps at most one progression member); exceptionalCount_lower_bound and exceptionalCount_positive_density combine these into a count of at least N/11184810 − (log₂ N + 1) exceptional integers below N, which exceeds N/22369620 once N ≥ 2^52; density_exceptionalSet_ge and lowerDensity_exceptionalSet_pos package this as 0 < lowerDensity ExceptionalSet.
sections.mathContext: The linear main term N/11184810 (one progression member per period) dwarfs the logarithmic loss log₂ N + 1 (trapped members) once N is large, giving a genuine positive-density lower bound rather than mere infinitude — Erdős's 1950 result at its full strength, proved unconditionally and axiom-free.

sections.title: Summary
sections.summary: Closing prose: Problem #16 is SOLVED (disproved by Chen 2023). Recap of Romanoff (1934, positive density are representable), Erdős (1950, exceptional set contains an AP with positive lower density — now proved at full strength, axiom-free), Chen (2023, not a single AP + noise); the exceptional set has small positive density (~0.09) and complex multi-progression structure. References including OEIS A006285.
sections.mathContext: Status recap: Erdős #16 disproved; the exceptional set has density $\approx 0.09$, contains arithmetic progressions via covering congruences (now proved to have positive lower density, not just infinitude), but is not captured by any single progression up to density 0.

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem #16 is DISPROVED (Chen 2023). The exceptional set of odd integers not representable as 2^k + p has more complex structure than Erdős conjectured. It's not just an arithmetic progression plus negligible noise - it contains multiple independent parts with positive density.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: The result shows that covering congruence constructions produce richer structure than expected.

The exceptional set may have fractal-like or quasi-random properties. This connects to deep questions about prime distribution.
openQuestions: What is the exact structure of the exceptional set?
Does the exceptional set have any self-similarity properties?

The covering progression alone gives a lower density of at least 1/22369620 (proved here, axiom-free); what is the precise density of the full exceptional set, accounting for Chen's additional independent progressions?
Are there infinitely many twin pairs (n, n+2) both exceptional?
